lastPrompt: find the root cause why RTL drops that address

content.text:
Done. The workaround is gone -- replaced by the real fix, verified end to end.

## Root cause (the RTL address drop)
`SimpleMemory` bounds-checked with `region.contains({addr, addr + len})`. The `{addr, addr+len}` temporary runs through `MemoryRegion`'s ctor, which treats arg 2 as an **inclusive** end and stores `end + 1`. Since `addr+len` is already the **exclusive** end, the temporary spanned `[addr, addr+len+1)` -- one byte too long -- so `contains()` rejected any access whose exclusive end landed on `end_address`: the final word of RAM, where x31's scratch slot sits.

## What I did (2 commits, branch `qemu-isa-match`, not pushed)
- **`05f2750` fix(mem)** -- added `MemoryRegion::contains_access(addr, len)`, a half-open check that does not round the end up, and used it in `SimpleMemory`. Strictly more permissive than before, so no fixture can regress. RED->GREEN via a `simple_memory` "final word" case + a `memory_region` unit case.
- **`a3a82ab` perf(hybrid)** -- dropped the x31 guard: block-load all 31 GPRs via the PB ld-sweep (x31 is the base, so its own `ld` is emitted last). 31 registers now cost 1 abstract write + ~5 PB executions instead of 31 abstract writes.

## Verification
- Full hybrid unit suite green natively. (`state_abi` fails on a **pre-existing v4-vs-v3 ABI skew** on this branch -- includes none of my files; `shared_mem_*` pass under the SystemC link recipe.)
- `--verify` byte-parity **PASS** on all 5: `rt_all_gprs` (the direct x31 proof -- 146 fields match), `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_c_matmul`.

Left untouched: the unrelated `external/systemc-cci` submodule bump and untracked `build_vsim.sh`. Say the word to push.

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

## Efficiency review: GPR block-load + memory-decoder diff

Net: the change is a big round-trip win (31 abstract writes -> ~6 DM round-trips). Two avoidable costs on the round-trip path, two negligible host-side nits, one improvement.

**1. `resume_driver.hpp:343` | reads `abstractcs` for progbufsize on every resume | avoidable DMI round-trip.**
`const uint32_t progbufsize = (bus_.read(kAbstractcs) >> 24)` runs on each resume. A `bus_.read()` is NOT free: `systemc_dmi_bus.hpp:31-36` busy-drains the AHB (`while(txn.is_busy()) sc_start`) until the DMI transaction completes -- a genuine debug-transport round-trip. progbufsize is a fixed DM property, invariant across resumes and constant within one. **Cheaper:** the codebase already hardcodes PB capacity as the compile-time constant `kProgbufMaxInsns = 15` (`program_buffer.hpp:29`); derive `max_lds` from that, or read once into a `static`/member cache. Saves 1 round-trip/resume.

**2. `resume_driver.hpp:344,348-354` | batch fill-factor may be half-optimal | up to 2 extra PB executions.**
The batching logic itself is correct and minimal: it packs `max_lds` loads/exec and the `k == 31` guard flushes the final partial batch with no trailing empty exec (verified: `n >= 1` at every `exec_progbuf`). But `max_lds = progbufsize - 1 = 7` (runtime value 8) gives 5 PB execs (7+7+7+7+3). The rest of the code assumes 15 payload slots (`kProgbufMaxInsns = 15`, i.e. a 16-entry buffer); at 15/exec the 31 loads collapse to **3 execs** (15+15+1). So the runtime `8` and the compile-time `15` disagree -- one is stale. If 15 is the real size, this wastes **2 busy-poll round-trips**; if 8 is real, `kProgbufMaxInsns = 15` is a latent over-count (exec of the 9-slot V-data sweep would overrun). **Cheaper:** reconcile to the true buffer size and batch at it. Ties into #1 -- fixing the constant removes the read AND the under-fill together.

**3. `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:147-148` | 31x 8-byte memcpy loop | negligible, cosmetic only.**
`state.gpr` is `uint64_t gpr[32]` (contiguous, `state_abi.h:192`) and the dest slots are contiguous at `off+(i-1)*8`, so this collapses to one `memcpy(ram.data()+off, &state.gpr[1], 31*8)`. The reviewer's "may not be contiguous" caveat does not apply -- source and dest orders match, single memcpy is valid. But this is host memory, 248 bytes, **zero DMI round-trips**. Not on the cost path; leave it or fold it, immaterial either way.

**4. `simulator.hpp:216` | `stage_gpr_to_scratch` called unconditionally | dead host memcpy on the fallback path (+ latent V corruption).**
Staging is not gated. When ResumeDriver takes the abstract-write fallback (`gpr_scratch_fits(vlenb)` false), the staged bytes are never read -> the 248-byte memcpy is wasted. Host-side, negligible cost, zero round-trips. **Guard that avoids it:** mirror ResumeDriver's own condition -- stage only when `hybrid::gpr_scratch_fits(hybrid_input_state_->vlenb)` (block-load is hardwired on here, so that fit check is the live gate). Worth adding not for the wasted memcpy but because the missing guard is also a correctness hazard: at large vlenb (e.g. 128, where V fills the entire 4096-byte page), this memcpy runs AFTER `stage_v_to_scratch` and overwrites the top 248 bytes = v30/v31. Same guard fixes both. (Flagging as the direct consequence of the asked-about missing guard, not a general bug hunt.)

**5. `memory_region.hpp:54` + `simple_memory.hpp:87-89` | `contains_access` vs old `contains({addr, addr+len})` | strictly cheaper, no concern.**
Old path constructed a temporary `MemoryRegion` (ctor does `end+1` and runs a `base > end` throw-check branch) then did 2 comparisons; the new `contains_access` does 3 scalar comparisons, no temporary, no ctor branch. Fewer ops per access, `[[likely]]` retained. This is an efficiency improvement, correctly the cheaper-or-equal the reviewer expected.</result>

if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

1	// Program Buffer execution helpers for the RISC-V Debug Module.
2	//
3	// Follows the same duck-typed template pattern as dmi_poll.hpp so that
4	// resume_driver.hpp can include this header without a circular dependency.
5	// Bus type requirement: write(uint8_t reg, uint32_t val) and
6	//                       read(uint8_t reg) -> uint32_t.
7	//
8	// Debug Spec references: section 3.6 (Program Buffer), table 3.1 (DMI),
9	// section 3.7.1.3 (Abstract Command - Access Register).
10	
11	#pragma once
12	
13	#include "hybrid/abstract_command.hpp"
14	#include "hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp"
15	
16	#include <array>
17	#include <cstdint>
18	#include <span>
19	#include <stdexcept>
20	#include <string>
21	
22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// DMI address of the first Program Buffer register (progbuf0..progbuf15).
25	inline constexpr uint8_t kProgbuf0 = 0x20u;
26	
27	// Max payload instructions: 16 total slots minus 1 reserved for the
28	// mandatory ebreak that terminates execution.
29	inline constexpr std::size_t kProgbufMaxInsns = 15u;
30	
31	// Standard ebreak encoding (funct12=1, opcode=SYSTEM).
32	inline constexpr uint32_t kEbreak = 0x00100073u;
33	
34	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
35	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
36	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
37	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
38	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
39	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
40	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
41	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
42	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
43	
44	// Encode `vsetvl rd, rs1, rs2` (RVV 1.0 section 6.2, funct7=1000000).
45	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,
46	// then branch-free-restore both in one Program Buffer execution.
47	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vsetvl(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, uint8_t rs2)
48	{
49	    return (0b1000000u << 25)
50	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
52	         | (0b111u << 12)
53	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
54	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
55	}
56	
57	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
58	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
59	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
60	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
61	{
62	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
63	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
64	         | (0b001u << 12)
65	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
66	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
67	}
68	
69	// Encode `vle8.v vd, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector load, EEW=8 (RVV 1.0 sec 7.4).
70	// Fields: vm=1 (unmasked, bit 25), width=000, mop=00, mew=0, nf=000,
71	// lumop=00000, opcode LOAD-FP=0x07. PB V-regfile reload sweeps v0..v31 from
72	// the shared scratch region after a vsetvl to e8/m1.
73	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vle8_v(uint8_t vd, uint8_t rs1)
74	{
75	    return (1u << 25)
76	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
77	         | ((uint32_t(vd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
78	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
79	}
80	
81	// Encode `vse8.v vs3, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector store, EEW=8. Mirror of
82	// encode_vle8_v with opcode STORE-FP=0x27. PB V-regfile dump sweeps v0..v31
83	// back to the shared scratch region at drain.
84	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vse8_v(uint8_t vs3, uint8_t rs1)
85	{
86	    return (1u << 25)
87	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
88	         | ((uint32_t(vs3) & 0x1Fu) << 7)
89	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
90	}
91	
92	// Encode `addi rd, rs1, imm12` (OP-IMM opcode 0x13, funct3=000). The batched
93	// V-data sweep advances the scratch base pointer x7 by one register-span
94	// between transfers WITHIN a Program-Buffer execution, so the per-register
95	// abstract x7 write disappears. imm12 is a signed 12-bit field (-2048..2047).
96	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_addi(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
97	{
98	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
99	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
100	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
101	         | 0x13u;  // OP-IMM opcode (funct3=000)
102	}
103	
104	// Encode `ld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD opcode 0x03, funct3=011 for 64-bit). The GPR
105	// block-load sweeps x1..x31 from a scratch region addressed by a base register,
106	// so 31 abstract register writes collapse into a few Program-Buffer executions.
107	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_ld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
108	{
109	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
110	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
111	         | (0b011u << 12)
112	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
113	         | 0x03u;  // LOAD opcode
114	}
115	
116	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
117	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
118	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
119	//
120	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
121	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
122	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
123	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
124	// surfacing the fault.
125	template<typename Bus>
126	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
127	{
128	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
129	        throw std::runtime_error(
130	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
131	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
132	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
133	
134	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
135	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
136	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
137	
138	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
139	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
140	
141	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
142	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
143	
144	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
145	    if (cmderr != 0u)
146	        throw std::runtime_error(
147	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
148	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
149	}
150	
151	// vtype encoding for e8, m8, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=011, vta=1, vma=1). The
152	// V-data sweep uses LMUL=8 so one vle8.v/vse8.v moves a whole group of 8
153	// registers (8*vlenb byte-elements, vl=8*vlenb) in a single instruction.
154	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u;
155	
156	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
157	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
158	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
159	template<typename Bus>
160	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
161	{
162	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
163	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
164	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
165	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
166	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
167	                     "write_register_abstract");
168	}
169	
170	// Sweep all 32 V data registers between the hart regfile and the vlenb-packed
171	// scratch region via the Program Buffer. load=true issues vle8.v
172	// (scratch -> regfile, on resume); load=false issues vse8.v (regfile ->
173	// scratch, at drain). The leading vsetvl to e8/m8 sets vl=8*vlenb and forces
174	// vstart=0, so one unit-stride access covers a whole LMUL=8 group of 8
175	// registers. Uses x5/x6 (vsetvl operands) and x7 (group base pointer) as
176	// scratch. `vlenb` is the runtime per-register width; the scratch must be
177	// packed at vlenb stride (stage_v_to_scratch) so each 8-register group is
178	// contiguous.
179	template<typename Bus>
180	inline void pb_v_data_sweep(Bus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa, uint64_t vlenb,
181	                            bool load)
182	{
183	    // The scratch holds v0..v31 packed contiguously at vlenb stride (see

lastPrompt: 所以 用program buffer 確實有比abstract command 快?

content.text:
Per single op: no. The win is batching, not a cheaper op.

Here is what the code actually costs. Every `bus.read`/`bus.write` runs one busy-poll (`drain()`), and the expensive part is the one hart round-trip where the DM runs the hart and polls `abstractcs.busy` until it re-halts (the ~1000-cycle wait the comments mention).

**One abstract command** (restore 1 register), `write_register_abstract`:
- write DATA0, write DATA1, write COMMAND, poll busy = ~4 DMI accesses, **1 hart round-trip**, moves **1 register**.

**One PB(8) execution** (7 insns + ebreak), `exec_progbuf`:
- 8 progbuf writes + cmderr read + COMMAND write + poll busy + final cmderr read = ~11 DMI accesses, **1 hart round-trip**, but can move **up to 7 registers** (7 `ld`s).

So per one execution, PB does *more* DMI traffic (it has to fill the buffer first). It is not cheaper than a single abstract command. They both pay one hart round-trip.

The reason the GPR block-load is faster is amortization - fewer round-trips for the same 31 registers:

| method | hart round-trips for 31 GPRs |
|--------|------------------------------|
| abstract, 1 reg each | 31 |
| PB block-load (7 loads/exec) | 1 seed + 5 execs = **~6** |

That is the ~5x cut. One PB round-trip carries 7 registers; one abstract round-trip carries 1.

The open question the profile answers: is PB's single round-trip the *same* cost as abstract's single round-trip, or a bit longer (the hart executes 8 insns instead of 1 abstract micro-op)? If PB's round-trip is longer, then batching is the *only* win and per-round-trip PB is actually slightly slower. That is exactly what I am measuring across the 4 engines - want me to finish the harness and get the hard numbers?

Only GPR and V-data use PB batching. FPR and every CSR are still one abstract command each.

From `resume_driver.hpp resume()`:

| block | count | method now | hart round-trips |
|-------|-------|-----------|------------------|
| **GPR** x1..x31 | 31 | **PB block-load** (`restore_gprs_via_pb`) | ~6 |
| **V data** v0..v31 | 32 | **PB grouped sweep** (`pb_v_data_sweep`) | ~2 (vsetvl + 1 exec) |
| **FPR** f0..f31 | 32 | abstract, one each | **32** |
| fcsr | 1 | abstract-first | 1 |
| mstatus | 1 | abstract-first | 1 |
| V-CSRs (vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr) | 4 | abstract-first | 4 |
| vtype+vl | 2 | PB (1 vsetvl) | 1 |
| dcsr/PMP (S/U only) | ~66 | abstract | ~66 |
| mtvec,mscratch,mepc,mcause,mtval,mie,mip | 7 | abstract | 7 |
| mcache_ctl,mmisc_ctl | 2 | abstract | 2 |
| Andes CSR block (+PMA) | ~13-31 | abstract (caps-gated) | ~13-31 |
| M-ext CSR block | varies | abstract (caps-gated) | varies |
| mcycle,minstret | 2 | abstract-first | 2 |
| DPC (pc) | 1 | abstract | 1 |

Note: `write_csr_abstract_or_pb` uses PB only as a *fallback* when the abstract write trips cmderr. The normal path is abstract, so "abstract-first" = 1 round-trip in the common case.

Key takeaway: **FPR is the biggest un-batched block - 32 round-trips.** It has the exact same shape as GPR (32 fixed-width regs), so the same trick applies: stage f0..f31 into the scratch page (host memcpy), then a PB `fld` sweep. That would cut ~32 round-trips to ~6, same as GPR.

CSRs are harder to batch - each needs a distinct `csr` immediate in a `csrrw`, and each is individually caps-gated / tolerant, so they do not collapse into one sweep as cleanly. The realistic batching targets are GPR (done), V-data (done), and **FPR (not done)**.

lastPrompt: does DMI abstract command support Burst Transfers?

content.text:
Confirmed from the code: the encoder here has only `postexec` (bit 18), not the postincrement bit, and nothing touches the `abstractauto` register. So this codebase uses no burst feature today.

**Answer: one abstract command = one transfer. No native burst. The spec adds optional burst-like *streaming*, but it would not beat the PB trick here.**

The RISC-V Debug spec gives two optional pieces that combine into a burst:

1. **postincrement** - `aarpostincrement` (bit 19, Access Register) or `aampostincrement` (Access Memory). After each access the DM auto-increments `regno`/address.
2. **`abstractauto`** register (0x18) - `autoexecdata`/`autoexecprogbuf`. Once set, touching `data0` re-runs the last command automatically.

Set the command once, then just hammer `data0` - each access auto-executes and steps to the next reg/word. That is the "burst."

Why it does not help our cost model:

| | abstract burst (autoexec + postinc) | PB `ld`/`fld` sweep |
|---|---|---|
| hart round-trips for N regs | **N** (each auto-exec is its own command + busy-poll) | **~N/7** (7 loads per execution) |
| payload path | through `data0`/`data1` over DMI | through **guest RAM** (the shared mmap) |
| what burst saves | only the per-reg `command` write (~1 DMI access) | - |

The burst only removes the `command`-register write each iteration. It still pays **one busy-poll per register**, and still ships every value through the narrow `data0`/`data1` DMI path. The PB sweep is better on both axes: it packs 7 transfers into one hart round-trip, and the register values ride the shared memory instead of DMI.

Two more caveats:
- Both features are **optional**. You would have to probe: write `abstractauto`, read back; if it does not stick, the Andes DM does not implement it. A `cmderr=2` ("not supported") on a postincrement command means the same.
- The one place burst genuinely wins is reading a large block of **guest memory** you cannot otherwise reach (Access Memory + `aampostincrement`). We do not have that problem - QEMU and vsim already share the mmap, so bulk data never needs DMI.

So: not worth pursuing for GPR/FPR/CSR restore. PB batching already beats it. The real remaining win is applying the PB sweep to **FPR** (still 32 round-trips).

1	/* rt_c_fcsr.c - Round-trip fixture: fcsr (frm + sticky fflags) across the
2	 * handoff (L20).
3	 *
4	 * Phase 1 (QEMU1): set fcsr = 0x21 (frm=RTZ(1)<<5 | fflags=NX) right
5	 *   before the enter marker; the plugin drains it into
6	 *   hybrid_state_v1.fcsr (offset 5456, locked by state_abi_check.h).
7	 * Phase 2 (vsim): ResumeDriver must restore fcsr before the ROI runs.
8	 *   The in-ROI self-check reads it back; on mismatch the fixture exits 1
9	 *   immediately, so the vsim leg returns 1 instead of 200 and the harness
10	 *   fails loudly. On success it writes the distinct sentinel 0x45
11	 *   (frm=RDN(2)<<5 | fflags=NX|UF) for StateDrain to capture at the exit
12	 *   marker -- the drained file's fcsr field must read 0x45
13	 *   (tests/hybrid/e2e_fcsr_roundtrip.sh asserts both file values).
14	 *
15	 * crt0.S sets mstatus.FS=Initial, so fcsr is writable in M-mode on both
16	 * engines. The insns after the exit marker (main's epilogue) touch no FP
17	 * state, so the drain's 0-3 insn halt slack cannot disturb the sentinel.
18	 */
19	#include <stdlib.h>
20	
21	#include "runtime/rt_c_helpers.h"
22	
23	int main(void)
24	{
25	  /* Phase 1 (QEMU1): non-default rounding mode + a sticky flag. */
26	  unsigned long set = 0x21; /* frm=RTZ | fflags=NX */
27	  asm volatile("csrw fcsr, %0" ::"r"(set));
28	
29	  enter_vsim();
30	
31	  /* Phase 2 (vsim): the restored fcsr must be intact. */
32	  unsigned long got;
33	  asm volatile("csrr %0, fcsr" : "=r"(got));
34	  if (got != 0x21)
35	    exit(1);
36	
37	  /* Leave a distinct value for the exit drain to capture. */
38	  unsigned long sentinel = 0x45; /* frm=RDN | fflags=NX|UF */
39	  asm volatile("csrw fcsr, %0" ::"r"(sentinel));
40	
41	  exit_vsim();
42	
43	  return 0;
44	}

// rt_all_gprs.S
//
// Tier-1 fixture: full sweep of x1..x31 across QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2.
// Each register survives the round-trip with its 64-bit value intact.
//
// Phase A (QEMU1):
//   x5 = 0x00002000 (also serves as Phase C spill base).
//   x_i = 0xA000_0000_0000_0000 + i for i in {1..4, 6..31}.
// Phase B (vsim):  no-op.
// Phase C (QEMU2):
//   Spill x6, x28, x29 (sacrificed below).
//   Verify x_i directly for i in {1..4, 7..27, 30..31, then 5}.
//   Verify spilled x6, x28, x29 against expected.
//   Exit code = first mismatching reg num, or 0 on full pass.

#include "semihost_exit.inc"

.section .text
.globl _start
_start:
    li      x6, 0xA000000000000000   // temp base for ADDI sweep
    addi    x1,  x6, 1
    addi    x2,  x6, 2
    addi    x3,  x6, 3
    addi    x4,  x6, 4
    addi    x7,  x6, 7
    addi    x8,  x6, 8
    addi    x9,  x6, 9
    addi    x10, x6, 10
    addi    x11, x6, 11
    addi    x12, x6, 12
    addi    x13, x6, 13
    addi    x14, x6, 14
    addi    x15, x6, 15
    addi    x16, x6, 16
    addi    x17, x6, 17
    addi    x18, x6, 18
    addi    x19, x6, 19
    addi    x20, x6, 20
    addi    x21, x6, 21
    addi    x22, x6, 22
    addi    x23, x6, 23
    addi    x24, x6, 24
    addi    x25, x6, 25
    addi    x26, x6, 26
    addi    x27, x6, 27
    addi    x28, x6, 28
    addi    x29, x6, 29
    addi    x30, x6, 30
    addi    x31, x6, 31
    addi    x6,  x6, 6               // x6 = 0xA000_..._6
    li      x5, 0x00002000           // x5 = spill base (also its expected value)

    slti   x0, x0,  0x5A0                 // QEMU1 drains, exits

    slti   x0, x0,  0x5A1                 // vsim drains, exits 200

phase_c:
    // Spill x6, x28, x29 to 0x00002000, +8, +16 before corrupting them.
    sd      x6,  0(x5)
    sd      x28, 8(x5)
    sd      x29, 16(x5)

    li      x6,  0xA000000000000000  // verification base
    li      x29, 0                   // result reg (0 = pass)

    .macro CHECK_BASE n
        bnez    x29, 99f
        addi    x28, x6, \n
        beq     x\n, x28, 99f
        addi    x29, x0, \n
    99:
    .endm

    CHECK_BASE 1
    CHECK_BASE 2
    CHECK_BASE 3
    CHECK_BASE 4
    CHECK_BASE 7
    CHECK_BASE 8
    CHECK_BASE 9
    CHECK_BASE 10
    CHECK_BASE 11
    CHECK_BASE 12
    CHECK_BASE 13
    CHECK_BASE 14
    CHECK_BASE 15
    CHECK_BASE 16
    CHECK_BASE 17
    CHECK_BASE 18
    CHECK_BASE 19
    CHECK_BASE 20
    CHECK_BASE 21
    CHECK_BASE 22
    CHECK_BASE 23
    CHECK_BASE 24
    CHECK_BASE 25
    CHECK_BASE 26
    CHECK_BASE 27
    CHECK_BASE 30
    CHECK_BASE 31

    // Verify x5 directly (still holds 0x00002000).
    bnez    x29, check_spilled
    li      x28, 0x00002000
    beq     x5, x28, check_spilled
    addi    x29, x0, 5

check_spilled:
    // Verify spilled x6 (expected = 0xA000_..._6).
    bnez    x29, check_x28
    ld      x28, 0(x5)
    li      x6, 0xA000000000000000
    addi    x6, x6, 6
    beq     x28, x6, check_x28
    addi    x29, x0, 6

check_x28:
    // Verify spilled x28 (expected = 0xA000_..._28).
    bnez    x29, check_x29
    ld      x28, 8(x5)
    li      x6, 0xA000000000000000
    addi    x6, x6, 28
    beq     x28, x6, check_x29
    addi    x29, x0, 28

check_x29:
    // Verify spilled x29 (expected = 0xA000_..._29).
    // Note: x29 is the result reg; if non-zero, skip but keep prior fail.
    bnez    x29, exit_build
    ld      x28, 16(x5)
    li      x6, 0xA000000000000000
    addi    x6, x6, 29
    beq     x28, x6, exit_build
    addi    x29, x0, 29

exit_build:
    mv      a2, x29
    SEMIHOST_EXIT a2

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md F3) ---------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md F3) ---------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

The biggest remaining win is the **drain side** - it is the exact mirror of what we just built, and it is still fully un-batched.

## The key gap: resume is batched, drain is not

We batched the 3 uniform register blocks on **resume** (GPR, FPR, V-data). But `StateDrain` reads them back **one register at a time** via abstract commands:

- `state_drain.hpp:55` - GPR readback: 31 abstract reads
- `state_drain.hpp:81` - FPR readback: 32 abstract reads

The code comment at `state_drain.hpp:162` even admits it: "~190 DMI abstract commands". The V-data drain already sweeps (`vse8.v`, line 197); GPR/FPR do not.

## Ranked PB targets

| # | Target | Now (round-trips) | After PB | When it applies | Effort |
|---|--------|------|------|------|------|
| 1 | **Drain GPR+FPR** (store-sweep) | 63 | ~12 | **every handoff** | low - mirrors done work |
| 2 | Resume PMP block | 72 | ~24 | S/U handoffs only | med |
| 3 | Resume/drain Andes PMA | 18 | ~6 | Andes cores | med |
| 4 | Scattered M-mode CSRs | ~15-28 | ~half | every handoff | high, low payoff |

## Why #1 is the clear next pick

It is the symmetric twin of the FPR work: always-on, same size, and it **reuses the scratch layout we already defined**. The store-sweep is `sd/fsd` regfile -> scratch (Program Buffer), then the host reads scratch straight from the shared mmap (a `memcpy`, zero hart round-trips) - just like `read_v_from_scratch` already does for V-data. New pieces are small: `encode_sd` + `encode_fsd` (mirror `encode_ld`/`encode_fld`), a `pb_block_store` helper (mirror `pb_block_load`), and `read_{gpr,fpr}_from_scratch`.

## Why CSRs (#2-4) batch worse than registers

A register sweep packs **7 loads per round-trip** (only rd + offset vary - one uniform `ld`). A CSR needs 2 instructions each (`ld xN, off; csrrw x0, <csr>, xN`) because the 12-bit CSR number is baked into the encoding and cannot be a runtime operand - so only **~3 CSRs per round-trip**. PMP (#2) is still worth it because 72 is large and the CSR numbers are consecutive (`pmpaddr0..63`), but it only fires on S/U handoffs, which the default M-mode engine never takes. #4 is not worth it - each CSR is individually caps-gated/tolerant, so the code cost is high for a small cut.

1	// Program Buffer execution helpers for the RISC-V Debug Module.
2	//
3	// Follows the same duck-typed template pattern as dmi_poll.hpp so that
4	// resume_driver.hpp can include this header without a circular dependency.
5	// Bus type requirement: write(uint8_t reg, uint32_t val) and
6	//                       read(uint8_t reg) -> uint32_t.
7	//
8	// Debug Spec references: section 3.6 (Program Buffer), table 3.1 (DMI),
9	// section 3.7.1.3 (Abstract Command - Access Register).
10	
11	#pragma once
12	
13	#include "hybrid/abstract_command.hpp"
14	#include "hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp"
15	
16	#include <array>
17	#include <cstdint>
18	#include <span>
19	#include <stdexcept>

22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// DMI address of the first Program Buffer register (progbuf0..progbuf15).
25	inline constexpr uint8_t kProgbuf0 = 0x20u;
26	
27	// Max payload instructions: 16 total slots minus 1 reserved for the
28	// mandatory ebreak that terminates execution.
29	inline constexpr std::size_t kProgbufMaxInsns = 15u;
30	
31	// Standard ebreak encoding (funct12=1, opcode=SYSTEM).
32	inline constexpr uint32_t kEbreak = 0x00100073u;
33	
34	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
35	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
36	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
37	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
38	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
39	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
40	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
41	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
42	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
43	
44	// Encode `vsetvl rd, rs1, rs2` (RVV 1.0 section 6.2, funct7=1000000).
45	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,
46	// then branch-free-restore both in one Program Buffer execution.
47	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vsetvl(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, uint8_t rs2)
48	{
49	    return (0b1000000u << 25)
50	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
52	         | (0b111u << 12)
53	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
54	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
55	}
56	
57	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
58	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
59	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
60	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
61	{
62	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
63	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
64	         | (0b001u << 12)
65	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
66	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
67	}
68	
69	// Encode `vle8.v vd, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector load, EEW=8 (RVV 1.0 sec 7.4).
70	// Fields: vm=1 (unmasked, bit 25), width=000, mop=00, mew=0, nf=000,
71	// lumop=00000, opcode LOAD-FP=0x07. PB V-regfile reload sweeps v0..v31 from
72	// the shared scratch region after a vsetvl to e8/m1.
73	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vle8_v(uint8_t vd, uint8_t rs1)
74	{
75	    return (1u << 25)
76	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
77	         | ((uint32_t(vd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
78	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
79	}
80	
81	// Encode `vse8.v vs3, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector store, EEW=8. Mirror of
82	// encode_vle8_v with opcode STORE-FP=0x27. PB V-regfile dump sweeps v0..v31
83	// back to the shared scratch region at drain.
84	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vse8_v(uint8_t vs3, uint8_t rs1)
85	{
86	    return (1u << 25)
87	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
88	         | ((uint32_t(vs3) & 0x1Fu) << 7)
89	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
90	}
91	
92	// Encode `addi rd, rs1, imm12` (OP-IMM opcode 0x13, funct3=000). The batched
93	// V-data sweep advances the scratch base pointer x7 by one register-span
94	// between transfers WITHIN a Program-Buffer execution, so the per-register
95	// abstract x7 write disappears. imm12 is a signed 12-bit field (-2048..2047).
96	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_addi(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
97	{
98	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
99	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
100	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
101	         | 0x13u;  // OP-IMM opcode (funct3=000)
102	}
103	
104	// Encode `ld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD opcode 0x03, funct3=011 for 64-bit). The GPR
105	// block-load sweeps x1..x31 from a scratch region addressed by a base register,
106	// so 31 abstract register writes collapse into a few Program-Buffer executions.
107	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_ld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
108	{
109	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
110	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
111	         | (0b011u << 12)
112	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
113	         | 0x03u;  // LOAD opcode
114	}
115	
116	// Encode `fld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD-FP opcode 0x07, funct3=011 for double). Same
117	// shape as encode_ld with the FP-load opcode: the FPR block-load sweeps f0..f31
118	// from the scratch region via an integer base register, collapsing 32 abstract
119	// FPR writes into a few Program-Buffer executions.
120	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_fld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
121	{
122	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
123	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
124	         | (0b011u << 12)
125	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
126	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
127	}
128	
129	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
130	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
131	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
132	//
133	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
134	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
135	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
136	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
137	// surfacing the fault.
138	template<typename Bus>
139	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
140	{
141	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
142	        throw std::runtime_error(
143	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
144	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
145	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
146	
147	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
148	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
149	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
150	
151	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
152	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
153	
154	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
155	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
156	
157	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
158	    if (cmderr != 0u)
159	        throw std::runtime_error(
160	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
161	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
162	}
163	
164	// vtype encoding for e8, m8, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=011, vta=1, vma=1). The
165	// V-data sweep uses LMUL=8 so one vle8.v/vse8.v moves a whole group of 8
166	// registers (8*vlenb byte-elements, vl=8*vlenb) in a single instruction.
167	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u;
168	
169	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
170	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
171	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
172	template<typename Bus>
173	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
174	{
175	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
176	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
177	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
178	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
179	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
180	                     "write_register_abstract");
181	}
182	
183	// Sweep all 32 V data registers between the hart regfile and the vlenb-packed
184	// scratch region via the Program Buffer. load=true issues vle8.v
185	// (scratch -> regfile, on resume); load=false issues vse8.v (regfile ->
186	// scratch, at drain). The leading vsetvl to e8/m8 sets vl=8*vlenb and forces
187	// vstart=0, so one unit-stride access covers a whole LMUL=8 group of 8
188	// registers. Uses x5/x6 (vsetvl operands) and x7 (group base pointer) as
189	// scratch. `vlenb` is the runtime per-register width; the scratch must be
190	// packed at vlenb stride (stage_v_to_scratch) so each 8-register group is
191	// contiguous.
192	template<typename Bus>
193	inline void pb_v_data_sweep(Bus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa, uint64_t vlenb,
194	                            bool load)
195	{
196	    // The scratch holds v0..v31 packed contiguously at vlenb stride (see
197	    // stage_v_to_scratch), so 8 consecutive registers form one LMUL=8 group.
198	    // One vle8.v/vse8.v then moves a whole group (8*vlenb contiguous bytes,
199	    // vl=8*vlenb) and all 32 registers transfer in 4 grouped ops -- whose 4
200	    // (transfer; addi) pairs fit in a SINGLE Program-Buffer execution. Each PB
201	    // execution is one halted-hart DM round-trip (~1000 sim cycles in the
202	    // busy-poll), so this is the floor: one vsetvl + one grouped execution. The
203	    // register bytes never cross DMI; they ride the shared mmap.
204	    constexpr unsigned     kRegsPerGroup   = 8;  // LMUL=8
205	    // kVtypeE8M8's vlmul field (bits 2:0) must encode this LMUL, so one grouped
206	    // vle8.v/vse8.v really covers kRegsPerGroup registers (integer LMUL=1<<vlmul;
207	    // 0xC3 & 7 == 3 -> LMUL 8).
208	    static_assert((1u << (kVtypeE8M8 & 0x7u)) == kRegsPerGroup,
209	                  "kVtypeE8M8 must encode LMUL = kRegsPerGroup");
210	    constexpr std::size_t  kGroupSweepInsns = (32 / kRegsPerGroup) * 2;  // (ld;addi)*4
211	    static_assert(kGroupSweepInsns <= kProgbufMaxInsns,
212	                  "the grouped sweep must fit one Program Buffer execution");
213	    const uint64_t group_bytes = static_cast<uint64_t>(kRegsPerGroup) * vlenb;
214	    if (group_bytes > 2047)  // addi imm12 is signed 12-bit; max 8*128 = 1024
215	        throw std::runtime_error(
216	            "pb_v_data_sweep: 8*vlenb exceeds the addi imm12 range");
217	
218	    // vsetvl to e8/m8 with AVL = 8*vlenb sets vl = VLMAX = 8*vlenb (one
219	    // byte-element per lane across the whole group) and forces vstart = 0.
220	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(5), group_bytes);  // AVL
221	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(6), kVtypeE8M8);   // e8, m8, ta, ma
222	    const std::array<uint32_t, 1> pb_vsetvl = { encode_vsetvl(0, 5, 6) };
223	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{pb_vsetvl});
224	
225	    // Base pointer x7 staged once; the in-buffer addi advances it one group at
226	    // a time. The group base register must be LMUL-aligned: v0/v8/v16/v24.
227	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(7), scratch_gpa);
228	    const uint32_t addi_step =
229	        encode_addi(7, 7, static_cast<int32_t>(group_bytes));
230	    std::array<uint32_t, kGroupSweepInsns> group_sweep{};
231	    std::size_t n = 0;
232	    for (uint8_t g = 0; g < 32; g += kRegsPerGroup) {
233	        group_sweep[n++] = load ? encode_vle8_v(g, 7) : encode_vse8_v(g, 7);
234	        group_sweep[n++] = addi_step;  // last group's addi is harmless dead work
235	    }
236	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{group_sweep.data(), n});
237	}

239	}  // namespace hybrid

2	// regfile transfer. The Debug Module abstract-command space has no slots for
3	// v0..v31 (the RISC-V Debug Spec leaves V to the Program Buffer or
4	// implementation-specific extensions), so vsim moves v0..v31 by executing a
5	// vle8.v/vse8.v sweep on the halted hart through the Program Buffer (see
6	// pb_v_data_sweep in program_buffer.hpp, driven by ResumeDriver on resume and
7	// StateDrain at drain). That sweep loads/stores the V scratch region of guest
8	// RAM -- the top page of the mapped span (v_scratch_gpa, L26); this header

37	// maximum supported VLEN; the actual per-reg byte count is `vlenb`. Defined in
38	// the shared ABI (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES) so the driver's mmap sizing and this
39	// consumer agree on one count (L26/F2).
40	inline constexpr std::size_t kVScratchBytes = HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES;
41	
42	// L26: the scratch region is the TOP kVScratchBytes of the mapped RAM span,
43	// not a fixed address. Scheme D parks it just above the program's declared
44	// RAM (the driver maps one page more than --mem-size), so no program layout
45	// can collide with it. This is the single source of truth for the GUEST
46	// address the Program-Buffer sweep (ResumeDriver/StateDrain) loads/stores
47	// through; the host stager below copies span-relative and needs no base.
48	inline constexpr auto v_scratch_gpa(uint64_t ram_base, std::size_t ram_size)
49	  -> uint64_t
50	{
51	  return ram_base + static_cast<uint64_t>(ram_size) - kVScratchBytes;
52	}

55	// it; a non-V handoff never consults the scratch GPA, so that is fine, but if
56	// a V handoff reaches the sweep with the GPA still unset the driver throws
57	// (loud) rather than silently transporting V through a bogus address.
58	inline constexpr uint64_t kVScratchGpaUnset =
59	  static_cast<uint64_t>(-1);

61	// GPR block-load prototype: x1..x31 (8 bytes each) staged in the TOP of the

64	// applies when the V data leaves room (gpr_scratch_fits), else the caller falls
65	// back to per-register abstract writes. A production version would give the GPR
66	// block its own scratch page instead of sharing the V one.
67	inline constexpr std::size_t kGprScratchBytes = 31 * 8;  // x1..x31
68	
69	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
70	{
71	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
72	}
73	
74	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
75	{
76	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
77	}

79	// FPR block-load: f0..f31 (8 bytes each) staged just BELOW the GPR block. Unlike
80	// x0, f0 is a real register, so all 32 f-regs ride the sweep (kFprScratchBytes =
81	// 32*8, not 31*8). The two blocks are disjoint and staged up front, so the FPR

83	// region grows up from the base, so the fit gate here is tighter than the GPR

101	// Byte offset of the scratch region inside a RAM span: its top page. Throws
102	// if the span is smaller than one scratch page (a too-small RAM mapping).
103	inline auto scratch_offset(std::size_t ram_size) -> std::size_t
104	{
105	  if (ram_size < kVScratchBytes)
106	    throw std::runtime_error(

117	                               std::span<uint8_t> ram)
118	{

120	  // Pack at vlenb stride (drop the wire-format padding) so v0..v31 sit
121	  // contiguously and the Program-Buffer sweep can move 8 at a time via LMUL=8.
122	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
123	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
124	    std::memcpy(ram.data() + off + r * vlenb,
125	                state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX, vlenb);
126	}

128	// Pack x1..x31 (8 bytes each) contiguously into the top kGprScratchBytes of the
129	// scratch page; the resume ld-sweep reads them back. state.gpr[1..31] is itself
130	// contiguous, so this is a single memcpy. Called before resume, gated by the
131	// caller on gpr_scratch_fits (the V region must leave room in the page).
132	inline void stage_gpr_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
133	                                 std::span<uint8_t> ram)
134	{
135	  const auto off =
136	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size()) + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes);
137	  std::memcpy(ram.data() + off, &state.gpr[1], 31 * 8);
138	}
139	
140	// Pack f0..f31 (8 bytes each) contiguously into the scratch page just below the
141	// GPR block; the resume fld-sweep reads them back. state.fpr[0..31] is itself
142	// contiguous, so this is a single memcpy. Called before resume, gated by the
143	// caller on fpr_scratch_fits (the V region must leave room for both blocks).
144	inline void stage_fpr_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
145	                                 std::span<uint8_t> ram)
146	{

content.content:
805	
806	With the QEMU2 handback removed, the code after your ROI never runs, so a
807	hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
808	(default OFF) cross-checks the run's correctness:
809	
810	```sh
811	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify your_prog.elf
812	# ...
813	# [marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
814	# [state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
815	# [verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
816	```
817	
818	Performance note: without `--verify`, the vsim leg drains only `mcycle`/`minstret`
819	(the cycle figure) and skips reading back the full architectural register file
820	over the Debug Module -- ~190 abstract commands (all FPRs, the vector-register
821	sweep, the Andes/M-ext CSR blocks) whose simulated debug cycles dominate hybrid
822	wall-clock for a short ROI but never affect the cycle count. `--verify` needs
823	every field for the diff, so it keeps the full drain; expect a `--verify` run to
824	take noticeably longer than the same run without it.
825	
826	How it works: after the normal run, the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the
827	oracle) with the plugin draining at the ROI exit boundary, sampled at the
828	exact pc where vsim halted. The pre-ROI path is QEMU in both runs, so the
829	ROI inputs are identical -- any architectural divergence inside the ROI
830	(RTL bug, state-restore bug, drain bug) shows up as a field mismatch and
831	the run exits non-zero, listing each differing field:
832	
833	```
834	[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
835	[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
836	```
837	
838	What is compared: pc, all GPRs, all FPRs (when FP state is live), the V
839	CSRs and full vector registers (when V state is live), and the writable
840	M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff -- `mscratch` (L23) and
841	`mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` (L24), restored at resume and re-read at
842	drain. What is not:
843	
844	- `mcycle`/`minstret` -- the engines count differently by design;
845	- `mip` -- restored and re-read, but its pending bits are hardware-driven

file.content:
With the QEMU2 handback removed, the code after your ROI never runs, so a
hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
(default OFF) cross-checks the run's correctness:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify your_prog.elf
# ...
# [marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
# [state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
# [verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
```

Performance note: without `--verify`, the vsim leg drains only `mcycle`/`minstret`
(the cycle figure) and skips reading back the full architectural register file
over the Debug Module -- ~190 abstract commands (all FPRs, the vector-register
sweep, the Andes/M-ext CSR blocks) whose simulated debug cycles dominate hybrid
wall-clock for a short ROI but never affect the cycle count. `--verify` needs
every field for the diff, so it keeps the full drain; expect a `--verify` run to
take noticeably longer than the same run without it.

How it works: after the normal run, the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the
oracle) with the plugin draining at the ROI exit boundary, sampled at the
exact pc where vsim halted. The pre-ROI path is QEMU in both runs, so the
ROI inputs are identical -- any architectural divergence inside the ROI
(RTL bug, state-restore bug, drain bug) shows up as a field mismatch and
the run exits non-zero, listing each differing field:

```
[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
```

What is compared: pc, all GPRs, all FPRs (when FP state is live), the V
CSRs and full vector registers (when V state is live), and the writable
M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff -- `mscratch` (L23) and
`mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` (L24), restored at resume and re-read at
drain. What is not:

- `mcycle`/`minstret` -- the engines count differently by design;
- `mip` -- restored and re-read, but its pending bits are hardware-driven
  (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which differs between QEMU's
  functional clock and vsim's cycle clock), so a compare would
  false-positive;
- `mstatus`, `mtvec` -- passthrough: vsim restores the QEMU1 entry snapshot value; both sides hold the same bits by construction so comparing is trivially true but not useful;

| drain readback | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| GPR | 31 abstract reads | 1 base capture + ~5 `sd` execs = **~6** |

content.text:
The register blocks are done. What's left is all CSRs - and they are a worse PB fit than GPR/FPR/V, so the returns diminish from here.

## What's still on abstract commands (per round-trip each)

| block | resume | drain | when | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PMP** (64 pmpaddr + 8 pmpcfg) | 72 | - | S/U handoffs only | consecutive CSRs, dense; ordering constraint (all addr before cfg) |
| **Andes V5** (13 scalars + 18 PMA) | ~caps subset | ~caps subset | every Andes core | PMA (pmaaddr0..15) consecutive; scalars scattered |
| **M-ext** (~17 on premium) | ~caps subset | ~caps subset | caps-gated | scattered addresses |
| scattered M-mode (mtvec/mscratch/mepc/mcause/mtval/mie/mip, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl) | ~9 | ~6 | every handoff | distinct addresses, no run |
| V scalar CSRs, fcsr, DPC, mstatus, counters | ~8 | ~9 | - | small, unavoidable |

## Why CSRs batch worse than registers

A GPR/FPR sweep packs **7 loads per round-trip** - one uniform `ld`, only rd+offset vary. A CSR cannot: the 12-bit CSR number is **baked into the `csrrw` encoding**, not a runtime operand. So each CSR needs `ld xN, off(base); csrrw x0, <csr>, xN` - **2 insns, ~3 CSRs per round-trip**, not 7.

Worse, there is a **fault-isolation** problem. Today each CSR restore is individually tolerant (`write_csr_tolerant` mirrors an unimplemented CSR as a no-op by clearing cmderr). Inside one PB execution you lose that: a single faulting `csrrw` raises cmderr and **kills the rest of the batch**. So a CSR sweep may only carry CSRs the caps say are implemented - which the Andes/M-ext blocks already gate on, but the scattered M-mode ones do not.

## The one clean lever left (altitude, not special-cases)

A **generic staged-CSR PB sweep**: `csr_sweep(bus, base, [(csr,value)...])` - stage values in scratch, emit `ld`+`csrrw` pairs batched at progbufsize-1, reuse for every caps-known block in both directions. That is the right shape (one primitive, not per-block hacks). Apply it to:

1. **Andes V5 + M-ext blocks** - the largest **always-present** consumer on the default engine, both directions. `~caps subset` each -> ~1/3. Best frequency.
2. **PMP block on resume** (72 -> ~24) - biggest single block, but **S/U-only**; the default M-mode engine never takes it.

## Honest recommendation

The high-value PB work is done. GPR+FPR+V were ~190 register moves -> ~36 round-trips (the sweet spot: uniform, large, always-present). The CSR tail is ~120 -> maybe ~45 at 3x, for more code and the fault-isolation caveat above. Real but second-order.

If you want to continue, build the one generic `csr_sweep` and point it at Andes+M-ext first (best frequency). If your workloads never use S/U mode, skip PMP. If they do, PMP is the biggest single win.
