# ROADMAP: liveness-gated transport (hybrid resume/drain)

Goal: stop paying Debug-Module traffic for state the program never changed.
Motivating profile (rt_c_hello, hybrid, --drain-minimal, ax45mpv_premium):
the vsim leg simulates 50,448 cycles for a 54-cycle ROI at ~9.8 kHz (5.2 s
wall). Split: Andes CSR block 15,235 cy / floor 13,334 cy / M-ext CSR block
9,622 cy / V transport 6,959 cy / FPR block 5,298 cy. Each DM operation
(abstract command or PB exec) costs ~200-900 simulated cycles.

Mechanism: compare each drained value against the ENGINE's own reset value
(a `hybrid_state_v1` baseline drained from the engine at reset). Equal means
the write is a no-op -- skip it. This is verify-transparent by construction
and self-heals QEMU-vs-engine reset divergence (msp_bound, milmb, ...).
mstatus-liveness (FS/VS == Off) was measured useless for C programs: hello
drains FS=Initial, VS=Clean with all-zero FPR/V data.

Known-limit notes:
- The opt-in CSR sweep (`set_csr_sweep`, currently OFF) bypasses the gate;
  filter its addr list by baseline before ever enabling it.
- Write-order hazards (mcounterwen gating counter writes) exist today in the
  tolerant path and are neither fixed nor worsened by gating; tracked by the
  separate caps/ordering audit (0x7D1 mis-gate).

## Features

### LG1: baseline-gated tolerant CSR restore -- state: DONE
- Description: `ResumeDriver::set_reset_baseline(state)` + skip every
  `write_csr_tolerant` call site (9 base scalars, Andes X-list, PMA loops,
  M-ext X-list) whose value equals the baseline. Never gated: mstatus, dpc,
  GPRs, mcycle, minstret, dcsr, S/U PMP mirror. `baseline_skip_count()`
  exposes the elision count for tests/logs. Dormant until LG3 wires a
  baseline in.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`,
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: none.

### LG2: baseline-gated FPR / V block skip -- state: TODO
- Description: skip the whole FPR fld-sweep + fcsr when fpr[0..31]+fcsr all
  equal the baseline; skip V staging + vle-sweep + vsetvl + vstart/vxsat/
  vxrm/vcsr when vreg bytes + V CSRs all equal the baseline. Decide whether
  the S/U PMP mirror joins the gate. Host-side staging (memcpy into scratch)
  may stay unconditional -- scratch is transport-only.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`, `src/simulator.hpp` (staging),
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1 (shares baseline plumbing + skip counter).

### LG3: reset-baseline capture + cache -- state: TODO
- Description: at hybrid resume the hart is freshly reset and halted -- the
  first run per engine build drains that reset state via StateDrain (~43k cy,
  one time), saves it under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/reset-<engine>-<version>
  .bin (validate magic/version + engine identity on load), and feeds it to
  ResumeDriver on every later run. `--no-reset-baseline` escape hatch.
  spdlog: cache hit/miss + skipped-write count.
- Key files: new `src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp` (key/path/load/save, unit-
  testable), `src/simulator.hpp` (`apply_resume_from_qemu`), `src/main.cpp`
  (flag), `tests/hybrid/reset_baseline.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1, LG2.

- Description: full `scripts/run_e2e.sh` + `--verify` matrix green; re-run
  the hello profile and record the new cycle split; update

  driver-side no code change expected.
- Key files: `andesim/docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `andesim/scripts/run_e2e.sh` logs.
- Dependencies: LG3.

stragglers), i.e. vsim leg ~5.2 s -> ~1.7 s, total run ~6.4 s -> ~2.3 s.

108	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). # ROADMAP: liveness-gated transport (hybrid resume/drain)

Goal: stop paying Debug-Module traffic for state the program never changed.
Motivating profile (rt_c_hello, hybrid, --drain-minimal, ax45mpv_premium):
the vsim leg simulates 50,448 cycles for a 54-cycle ROI at ~9.8 kHz (5.2 s
wall). Split: Andes CSR block 15,235 cy / floor 13,334 cy / M-ext CSR block
9,622 cy / V transport 6,959 cy / FPR block 5,298 cy. Each DM operation
(abstract command or PB exec) costs ~200-900 simulated cycles.

Mechanism: compare each drained value against the ENGINE's own reset value
(a `hybrid_state_v1` baseline drained from the engine at reset). Equal means
the write is a no-op -- skip it. This is verify-transparent by construction
and self-heals QEMU-vs-engine reset divergence (msp_bound, milmb, ...).
mstatus-liveness (FS/VS == Off) was measured useless for C programs: hello
drains FS=Initial, VS=Clean with all-zero FPR/V data.

Known-limit notes:
- The opt-in CSR sweep (`set_csr_sweep`, currently OFF) bypasses the gate;
  filter its addr list by baseline before ever enabling it.
- Write-order hazards (mcounterwen gating counter writes) exist today in the
  tolerant path and are neither fixed nor worsened by gating; tracked by the
  separate caps/ordering audit (0x7D1 mis-gate).

## Features

### LG1: baseline-gated tolerant CSR restore -- state: DONE
- Description: `ResumeDriver::set_reset_baseline(state)` + skip every
  `write_csr_tolerant` call site (9 base scalars, Andes X-list, PMA loops,
  M-ext X-list) whose value equals the baseline. Never gated: mstatus, dpc,
  GPRs, mcycle, minstret, dcsr, S/U PMP mirror. `baseline_skip_count()`
  exposes the elision count for tests/logs. Dormant until LG3 wires a
  baseline in.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`,
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: none.

### LG2: baseline-gated FPR / V block skip -- state: DONE
- Description: skip the whole FPR fld-sweep + fcsr when fpr[0..31]+fcsr all
  equal the baseline; skip V staging + vle-sweep + vsetvl + vstart/vxsat/
  vxrm/vcsr when vreg bytes + V CSRs all equal the baseline. Decide whether
  the S/U PMP mirror joins the gate. Host-side staging (memcpy into scratch)
  may stay unconditional -- scratch is transport-only.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`, `src/simulator.hpp` (staging),
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1 (shares baseline plumbing + skip counter).

### LG3: reset-baseline capture + cache -- state: DONE
- Landed notes: cache key adds the ELF identity (the hart free-runs a few
  workload insns before the DMI halt, so the halted state is per-ELF);
  capture enables mstatus.FS/VS first (reset leaves them Off and the
  fsd/vse8 capture sweeps fault otherwise); capture runs pass
  v_cfg_at_reset=false (the capture V sweep clobbers vtype/vl/vstart).
- Description: at hybrid resume the hart is freshly reset and halted -- the
  first run per engine build drains that reset state via StateDrain (~43k cy,
  one time), saves it under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/reset-<engine>-<version>
  .bin (validate magic/version + engine identity on load), and feeds it to
  ResumeDriver on every later run. `--no-reset-baseline` escape hatch.
  spdlog: cache hit/miss + skipped-write count.
- Key files: new `src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp` (key/path/load/save, unit-
  testable), `src/simulator.hpp` (`apply_resume_from_qemu`), `src/main.cpp`
  (flag), `tests/hybrid/reset_baseline.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1, LG2.

### LG4: e2e proof + docs (andesim repo) -- state: TODO
- Description: full `scripts/run_e2e.sh` + `--verify` matrix green; re-run
  the hello profile and record the new cycle split; update
  `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` (first-run baseline capture note, escape hatch);
  driver-side no code change expected.
- Key files: `andesim/docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `andesim/scripts/run_e2e.sh` logs.
- Dependencies: LG3.

Measured result for hello (LG3 landed): cache-hit vsim leg 12,258 cycles /
1.15 s (was 50,448 / 5.2 s; 114 restores elided), whole hybrid run 6.4 s ->
1.4 s. Capture run: 59,911 cycles, paid once per (engine build, ELF).
--verify passes with the gate active (146 fields).

- `3380953` test: state_abi contract updated to the shipped v4 wire format (pre-existing failure, fixed first so every later commit is green)
- `8293afb` perf: the previous session's uncommitted block-transport work, committed on its own as you asked — LG1 was reversed out of the files first, then restored byte-identical (sha256-checked)

## Two real bugs the TDD tests caught during design

1. **Clobber rule**: the V-data sweep's own `vsetvl` overwrites vtype/vl/vstart, so "value equals baseline" stops being true mid-restore — the architectural vsetvl may only be skipped when the data sweep was also skipped. Same rule applies to capture runs (`v_cfg_at_reset=false`).

- vsim repo: `config.yaml` (your local 2-engine build trim) and the `external/systemc-cci` submodule content — both pre-existing.
- andesim repo: my doc updates (USER_GUIDE 2.4 gate section + `--no-reset-baseline` row, CLAUDE.md ResumeDriver bullet) sit in files that already had your uncommitted edits, so I left them for you to commit together.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Hybrid handoff: QEMU1 (fast, drains `hybrid_state_v1` at ROI marker) → vsim (cycle-accurate; resume via RISC-V Debug Module DMI abstract commands + Program Buffer; run ROI; drain). Cycle figure = vsim mcycle delta.
   - Profiling result: each DM operation (abstract command or PB exec) costs ~200-900 simulated cycles at ~10 kHz sim speed; vsim leg = 50,448 cycles for a 54-cycle ROI (hello). Split: Andes CSRs 15,235 / floor 13,334 / M-ext CSRs 9,622 / V 6,959 / FPR 5,298. Full drain 93,720 cy. Cycle-mode whole hello = 4,340 cy.
   - Liveness gate (reset baseline): skip any restore whose drained value equals the engine's own reset value (no-op write; verify-transparent by construction; self-heals QEMU-vs-engine reset divergence like msp_bound/milmb).
   - Plugin sets flags (FP/V/ANDES/M_EXT) from QEMU capability, NOT program usage — hello drains flags=0x1f with FS=Initial, VS=Clean, all-zero FPR/vreg, vtype=0x8000000000000000 (vill), vl=0.

# ROADMAP: liveness-gated transport (hybrid resume/drain)

Goal: stop paying Debug-Module traffic for state the program never changed.
Motivating profile (rt_c_hello, hybrid, --drain-minimal, ax45mpv_premium):
the vsim leg simulates 50,448 cycles for a 54-cycle ROI at ~9.8 kHz (5.2 s
wall). Split: Andes CSR block 15,235 cy / floor 13,334 cy / M-ext CSR block
9,622 cy / V transport 6,959 cy / FPR block 5,298 cy. Each DM operation
(abstract command or PB exec) costs ~200-900 simulated cycles.

Mechanism: compare each drained value against the ENGINE's own reset value
(a `hybrid_state_v1` baseline drained from the engine at reset). Equal means
the write is a no-op -- skip it. This is verify-transparent by construction
and self-heals QEMU-vs-engine reset divergence (msp_bound, milmb, ...).
mstatus-liveness (FS/VS == Off) was measured useless for C programs: hello
drains FS=Initial, VS=Clean with all-zero FPR/V data.

Known-limit notes:
- The opt-in CSR sweep (`set_csr_sweep`, currently OFF) bypasses the gate;
  filter its addr list by baseline before ever enabling it.
- Write-order hazards (mcounterwen gating counter writes) exist today in the
  tolerant path and are neither fixed nor worsened by gating; tracked by the
  separate caps/ordering audit (0x7D1 mis-gate).

## Features

### LG1: baseline-gated tolerant CSR restore -- state: DONE
- Description: `ResumeDriver::set_reset_baseline(state)` + skip every
  `write_csr_tolerant` call site (9 base scalars, Andes X-list, PMA loops,
  M-ext X-list) whose value equals the baseline. Never gated: mstatus, dpc,
  GPRs, mcycle, minstret, dcsr, S/U PMP mirror. `baseline_skip_count()`
  exposes the elision count for tests/logs. Dormant until LG3 wires a
  baseline in.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`,
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: none.

### LG2: baseline-gated FPR / V block skip -- state: DONE
- Description: skip the whole FPR fld-sweep + fcsr when fpr[0..31]+fcsr all
  equal the baseline; skip V staging + vle-sweep + vsetvl + vstart/vxsat/
  vxrm/vcsr when vreg bytes + V CSRs all equal the baseline. Decide whether
  the S/U PMP mirror joins the gate. Host-side staging (memcpy into scratch)
  may stay unconditional -- scratch is transport-only.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`, `src/simulator.hpp` (staging),
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1 (shares baseline plumbing + skip counter).

### LG3: reset-baseline capture + cache -- state: DONE
- Landed notes: cache key adds the ELF identity (the hart free-runs a few
  workload insns before the DMI halt, so the halted state is per-ELF);
  capture enables mstatus.FS/VS first (reset leaves them Off and the
  fsd/vse8 capture sweeps fault otherwise); capture runs pass
  v_cfg_at_reset=false (the capture V sweep clobbers vtype/vl/vstart).
- Description: at hybrid resume the hart is freshly reset and halted -- the
  first run per engine build drains that reset state via StateDrain (~43k cy,
  one time), saves it under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/reset-<engine>-<version>
  .bin (validate magic/version + engine identity on load), and feeds it to
  ResumeDriver on every later run. `--no-reset-baseline` escape hatch.
  spdlog: cache hit/miss + skipped-write count.
- Key files: new `src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp` (key/path/load/save, unit-
  testable), `src/simulator.hpp` (`apply_resume_from_qemu`), `src/main.cpp`
  (flag), `tests/hybrid/reset_baseline.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1, LG2.

### LG4: e2e proof + docs (andesim repo) -- state: DONE
- Landed notes: full suite green with the gate live and a cold cache
  (47/47: marker 23, pc 23, neg 1); `--verify` PASS (146 fields);
  USER_GUIDE 2.4 documents the gate, `--no-reset-baseline`, and the cache
  location; andesim CLAUDE.md ResumeDriver bullet updated.
- Description: full `scripts/run_e2e.sh` + `--verify` matrix green; re-run
  the hello profile and record the new cycle split; update
  `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` (first-run baseline capture note, escape hatch);
  driver-side no code change expected.
- Key files: `andesim/docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `andesim/scripts/run_e2e.sh` logs.
- Dependencies: LG3.

Measured result for hello (LG3 landed): cache-hit vsim leg 12,258 cycles /
1.15 s (was 50,448 / 5.2 s; 114 restores elided), whole hybrid run 6.4 s ->
1.4 s. Capture run: 59,911 cycles, paid once per (engine build, ELF).
--verify passes with the gate active (146 fields).

It is one wrong line in the CSR capability table that makes the fast batch-transfer path (the CSR sweep) crash, so the sweep is turned off today.

**The bug** (`andes_caps.hpp:72`): `andes_caps.hpp` is the table that says "this engine has CSR X, yes/no". For CSR `0x7D1` (`mcountermask_m`) it checks the wrong feature:

```cpp
case 0x7D1: return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;   // mcountermask_m  <- WRONG
...
case 0x30A: case 0x306: case 0x7D3:           // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u
case 0x7CE:                                   // mcounterwen
    return AndesGate::UMODE;                  // <- its twins use the right gate
```

The Andes spec says `mcountermask_m` exists only when the core has **User mode** (plus the perf-monitor feature). The premium engine is M-mode-only (`NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) but has the perf-monitor interrupt on, so the table wrongly answers "yes, 0x7D1 exists". Its twin CSRs `0x7D3` and `0x7CE` already use the correct `UMODE` gate - `0x7D1` was just left in the wrong group.

**Why it blocks the sweep**: the CSR sweep packs many CSRs into one Program Buffer run (`csrr` + `sd` pairs, values ride the scratch page) - about 10x fewer DM operations than one abstract command per CSR. But one PB run is all-or-nothing: if any single `csrr` hits a CSR the hart does not really have, the hart raises illegal-instruction, the whole run fails with `cmderr=3`, and the code throws. The one-by-one abstract path can tolerate a bad CSR (skip it); the sweep cannot. Because the table over-claims `0x7D1`, the sweep would always crash on premium - so it was built but left disabled.

**The plan** ("then enable the CSR sweep"):
1. Fix the gate: move `0x7D1` into the `UMODE` group (RED test first: M-only config must report `supports_csr(0x7D1) == false`).
2. With the table now exact, turn the sweep on for the drain side (reading CSRs back at exit - `csrr` on a real CSR never faults) and add the missing lift of swept values from the scratch page.
3. Keep the restore side one-by-one for now (writing via `csrrw` can still fault on read-only fields - separate audit).
4. Make the sweep respect the LG1 liveness gate (filter its CSR list by the reset baseline), so the two optimizations do not fight.

The payoff is the next chunk of the remaining 12.3k-cycle floor: full drains (used by `--verify`) still pay one abstract command per CSR; the sweep batches them.

Want me to start with the RED test for the gate fix?

1	// Andes-CSR capability gating.
2	//
3	// A core implements an Andes custom CSR only when the matching feature is
4	// configured into it (config.inc). Restoring a CSR the target core lacks can
5	// hang the DMI handshake -- observed on ax45mpv_premium for ucode (no DSP) and
6	// mecc_code (no ECC). So the resume/drain loops transport only the CSRs the
7	// target core supports, decided here from the core's feature gates.
8	//
9	// This header is Verilator/SystemC-free: it maps a CSR address to its gate and
10	// answers "does a core with these gates support this CSR". The binding of each
11	// gate to the core's compiled-in `_NDS_*` config macros lives in the sim binary
12	// (see andes_caps_from_config), so this stays unit-testable in isolation.
13	#ifndef ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
14	#define ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <string>
18	#include <vector>
19	
20	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
21	
22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// The hardware feature that gates each transported CSR. ALWAYS = unconditionally
25	// present (a base machine CSR every core has; never gated off). The first block
26	// gates the v3 Andes custom CSRs; the second block (UMODE..TRIGGER) gates the v4
27	// M-ext CSRs (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST) -- standard + Andes M-mode CSRs whose
28	// existence depends on a privilege level or extension the core may not have.
29	enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
30	  ALWAYS = 0,
31	  DSP,
32	  CODENSE,
33	  POWERBRAKE,
34	  STACKSAFE,
35	  ECC,
36	  PMA,
37	  ILM,
38	  DLM,
39	  PERF_MONITOR,
40	  // v4 M-ext gates.
41	  UMODE,       // needs U-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
42	  SMODE,       // needs S-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS == 3)
43	  EPMP,        // ePMP / Smepmp (mseccfg)
44	  SMRNMI,      // resumable NMI (mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec)
45	  EXCSLVL,     // exception save levels (msave*)
46	  CLIC,        // CLIC / enhanced CLIC (mtvt/mintthresh/mcirq_entry)
47	  SMSTATEEN,   // state-enable (mstateen0..3)
48	  CCTL,        // cache control CSRs (mcctlbeginaddr/mcctldata)
49	  PPI,         // private peripheral interface base (mppib)
50	  FIO,         // fast IO base (mfiob)
51	  TRIGGER,     // debug triggers (tselect/tdata1/tdata2/tcontrol/mcontext)
52	};
53	
54	// Map an Andes CSR (by address) to the feature gate that enables it. Addresses
55	// are the HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST scalars plus the PMA block. A CSR with no
56	// custom-extension gate is ALWAYS (a base machine CSR every Andes core has).
57	// Maintainer note: a CSR added to HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST that needs gating must
58	// get a case here, else it defaults to ALWAYS (transported unconditionally).
59	constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr)
60	{
61	  switch (csr_addr) {
62	    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode (DSP overflow flag)
63	    case 0x800: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // uitb  (CoDense table base)
64	    case 0x017: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // jvt   (Zcmt/CoDense)
65	    case 0x7C5: return AndesGate::POWERBRAKE;     // mpft_ctl
66	    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;            // mecc_code
67	    case 0x7C6:                                   // mhsp_ctl
68	    case 0x7C7:                                   // msp_bound
69	    case 0x7C8: return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;      // msp_base
70	    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;            // milmb (ILM base)
71	    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;            // mdlmb (DLM base)
72	    case 0x7D1: return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;   // mcountermask_m
73	    // v4 M-ext CSR gates (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST).
74	    // mcounterwen (0x7CE) and mcountermask_u (0x7D3) need user mode (spec
75	    // existence: PMNDS & misa[20]); on an M-only core they WARL to 0, so gate
76	    // them UMODE -- not PERF_MONITOR -- or a restore writes a value the RTL
77	    // drops, false-diffing --verify.
78	    case 0x30A: case 0x306: case 0x7D3:           // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u
79	    case 0x7CE:                                   // mcounterwen
80	    case 0x808: case 0x80B: case 0x811: case 0x813:  // uzobctl, ucctlbeginaddr, sleepvalue, umisc_ctl
81	      return AndesGate::UMODE;
82	    case 0x7D2: case 0x7D5: return AndesGate::SMODE;  // mcountermask_s, mslideleg
83	    case 0x747: return AndesGate::EPMP;           // mseccfg
84	    case 0x320: case 0xB03: case 0xB04: case 0xB05: case 0xB06:  // mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6
85	    case 0x323: case 0x324: case 0x325: case 0x326:              // mhpmevent3-6
86	    case 0x7CF:                                                  // mcounterinten (PMNDS only)
87	      return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;
88	    case 0x740: case 0x741: case 0x742: case 0x744:  // mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus
89	    case 0x7C3: case 0x7DE:                           // mnvec, mrnxvec
90	      return AndesGate::SMRNMI;
91	    case 0x7C9: return AndesGate::ALWAYS;         // mdcause (base Andes trap CSR)
92	    case 0x7D6: case 0x7D7: case 0x7D8: case 0x7D9:  // msavestatus, msaveepc1, msavecause1, msaveepc2
93	    case 0x7DA: case 0x7DB: case 0x7DC:              // msavecause2, msavedcause1, msavedcause2
94	      return AndesGate::EXCSLVL;
95	    case 0x307: case 0x347: case 0x7EC:           // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
96	      return AndesGate::CLIC;
97	    case 0x30C: case 0x30D: case 0x30E: case 0x30F:  // mstateen0..3
98	      return AndesGate::SMSTATEEN;
99	    case 0x7CB: case 0x7CD: return AndesGate::CCTL;  // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
100	    case 0x7F0: return AndesGate::PPI;            // mppib
101	    case 0x7F1: return AndesGate::FIO;            // mfiob
102	    case 0x7A0: case 0x7A1: case 0x7A2: case 0x7A5: case 0x7A8:  // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
103	      return AndesGate::TRIGGER;
104	    default:
105	      // PMA cfg (0xBC0, 0xBC2) and addr (0xBD0..0xBDF) blocks.
106	      if (csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR || csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2)
107	        return AndesGate::PMA;
108	      if (csr_addr >= HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR &&
109	          csr_addr < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM)
110	        return AndesGate::PMA;
111	      return AndesGate::ALWAYS;                    // mxstatus 0x7C4, mclk_ctl 0x7DF
112	  }
113	}
114	
115	// The set of Andes feature gates a target core has on. Built from the core's
116	// compiled-in config (config.inc) in the sim binary and injected into the
117	// resume/drain loops, so they transport only the CSRs the core implements.
118	// Default = every gate on (all(): no gating, the prior unconditional behavior).
119	struct AndesCaps {
120	  uint32_t gate_mask = ~0u;
121	
122	  static constexpr AndesCaps all()  { return AndesCaps{~0u}; }
123	  static constexpr AndesCaps none() { return AndesCaps{0u}; }
124	
125	  constexpr void set(AndesGate g, bool on = true)
126	  {
127	    const uint32_t bit = 1u << static_cast<unsigned>(g);
128	    if (on) gate_mask |= bit;
129	    else    gate_mask &= ~bit;
130	  }
131	
132	  constexpr bool gate_on(AndesGate g) const
133	  {
134	    return (gate_mask >> static_cast<unsigned>(g)) & 1u;
135	  }
136	
137	  // ALWAYS-gated CSRs are present on every core regardless of the mask.
138	  constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const
139	  {
140	    const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);
141	    return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);
142	  }
143	};
144	
145	// The gated CSR names this core supports, for the --describe card. Iterates the
146	// two single-source-of-truth X-macro lists: the v3 Andes custom CSRs and the v4
147	// M-ext CSRs. The driver uses this list to gate --verify, so a CSR the core
148	// lacks is neither restored, drained, nor compared.
149	inline std::vector<std::string> supported_andes_csr_names(const AndesCaps& caps)
150	{
151	  std::vector<std::string> out;
152	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
153	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
154	#undef X
155	  // PMA group markers (whole pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] blocks share one gate), so a
156	  // consumer can include/exclude PMA without listing all 18 entries.
157	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR))  out.push_back("pmacfg");
158	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR)) out.push_back("pmaaddr");
159	  // v4 M-ext CSRs share the same address->gate map and --describe list.
160	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
161	  HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
162	#undef X
163	  return out;
164	}
165	
166	}  // namespace hybrid
167	
168	#endif  // ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
169

// Build an AndesCaps from the core's compiled-in config.inc feature macros
// (_NDS_*, supplied by the build-generated cpu_config.hpp). This is the ONE
// place that binds each Andes feature gate to its config macro -- the sim-binary
// counterpart of the Verilator-free andes_caps.hpp, kept separate so the unit
// tests never need the generated header.
//
// PRECONDITION: the _NDS_* macros must already be in scope (include this AFTER
// cpu_config.hpp). A macro that is absent reads as "feature off" (gate clear),
// never a compile error -- so a core whose config omits a knob stays safe.
#pragma once

#include "hybrid/andes_caps.hpp"

namespace hybrid {

inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config()
{
  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();

#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);           // ucode
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::CODENSE);       // uitb, jvt
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::POWERBRAKE);    // mpft_ctl
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);     // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT) && _NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR);  // mcountermask_m
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES) && (_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::PMA);           // pmacfg / pmaaddr
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::ILM);           // milmb
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::DLM);           // mdlmb
#endif
  // ECC: mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC.
#if (defined(_NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
    (defined(_NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
    (defined(_NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    || \
    (defined(_NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)
  c.set(AndesGate::ECC);           // mecc_code
#endif

  // v4 M-ext gates. Privilege-level gates from NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS
  // (1 = M, 2 = M+U, 3 = M+S+U). An absent knob reads as off -- safe.
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);         // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u, U-delta
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3)
  c.set(AndesGate::SMODE);         // mcountermask_s, mslideleg
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER) && (_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::TRIGGER);       // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_SMEPMP) && _NDS_SMEPMP) || (defined(_NDS_EPMP) && _NDS_EPMP)
  c.set(AndesGate::EPMP);          // mseccfg
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_SMRNMI) && _NDS_SMRNMI) || (defined(_NDS_RNMI) && _NDS_RNMI)
  c.set(AndesGate::SMRNMI);        // mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_EXCSLVL) && (_NDS_EXCSLVL > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::EXCSLVL);       // msave*
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_ECLIC) && _NDS_ECLIC) || (defined(_NDS_CLIC) && _NDS_CLIC)
  c.set(AndesGate::CLIC);          // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_SMSTATEEN) && _NDS_SMSTATEEN
  c.set(AndesGate::SMSTATEEN);     // mstateen0..3
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_CCTLCSR) && _NDS_CCTLCSR) || (defined(_NDS_CCTL) && _NDS_CCTL)
  c.set(AndesGate::CCTL);          // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::PPI);           // mppib
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB > 0)) || \
    (defined(_NDS_FIO) && _NDS_FIO)
  c.set(AndesGate::FIO);           // mfiob
#endif

  return c;
}

}  // namespace hybrid

// Build an AndesCaps from the core's compiled-in config.inc feature macros
// (_NDS_*, supplied by the build-generated cpu_config.hpp). This is the ONE
// place that binds each Andes feature gate to its config macro -- the sim-binary
// counterpart of the Verilator-free andes_caps.hpp, kept separate so the unit
// tests never need the generated header.
//
// PRECONDITION: the _NDS_* macros must already be in scope (include this AFTER
// cpu_config.hpp). A macro that is absent reads as "feature off" (gate clear),
// never a compile error -- so a core whose config omits a knob stays safe.
#pragma once

#include "hybrid/andes_caps.hpp"

namespace hybrid {

inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config()
{
  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();

#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);           // ucode
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::CODENSE);       // uitb, jvt
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::POWERBRAKE);    // mpft_ctl
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);     // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT) && _NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR);  // mcountermask_m
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES) && (_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::PMA);           // pmacfg / pmaaddr
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::ILM);           // milmb
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::DLM);           // mdlmb
#endif
  // ECC: mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC.
#if (defined(_NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
    (defined(_NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
    (defined(_NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    || \
    (defined(_NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)
  c.set(AndesGate::ECC);           // mecc_code
#endif

  // v4 M-ext gates. Privilege-level gates from NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS
  // (1 = M, 2 = M+U, 3 = M+S+U). An absent knob reads as off -- safe.
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);         // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u, U-delta
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3)
  c.set(AndesGate::SMODE);         // mcountermask_s, mslideleg
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER) && (_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::TRIGGER);       // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_SMEPMP) && _NDS_SMEPMP) || (defined(_NDS_EPMP) && _NDS_EPMP)
  c.set(AndesGate::EPMP);          // mseccfg
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_SMRNMI) && _NDS_SMRNMI) || (defined(_NDS_RNMI) && _NDS_RNMI)
  c.set(AndesGate::SMRNMI);        // mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_EXCSLVL) && (_NDS_EXCSLVL > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::EXCSLVL);       // msave*
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_ECLIC) && _NDS_ECLIC) || (defined(_NDS_CLIC) && _NDS_CLIC)
  c.set(AndesGate::CLIC);          // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_SMSTATEEN) && _NDS_SMSTATEEN
  c.set(AndesGate::SMSTATEEN);     // mstateen0..3
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_CCTLCSR) && _NDS_CCTLCSR) || (defined(_NDS_CCTL) && _NDS_CCTL)
  c.set(AndesGate::CCTL);          // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::PPI);           // mppib
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB > 0)) || \
    (defined(_NDS_FIO) && _NDS_FIO)
  c.set(AndesGate::FIO);           // mfiob
#endif

  return c;
}

}  // namespace hybrid

154	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)

156	}
157	
158	// Encode `fsd rs2, imm12(rs1)` (STORE-FP opcode 0x27, funct3=011 for double).
159	// Same S-type shape as encode_sd with the FP-store opcode: the FPR drain sweeps
160	// f0..f31 from the regfile into the scratch region via an integer base register.
161	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_fsd(uint8_t rs2, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
162	{
163	    const uint32_t imm = uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu;
164	    return ((imm >> 5) & 0x7Fu) << 25
165	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
166	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
167	         | (0b011u << 12)
168	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)
169	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
170	}
171	
172	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
173	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
174	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
175	//
176	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
177	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
178	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
179	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
180	// surfacing the fault.
181	template<typename Bus>
182	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
183	{
184	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
185	        throw std::runtime_error(
186	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
187	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
188	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
189	
190	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
191	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
192	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
193	
194	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
195	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
196	
197	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
198	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
199	
200	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
201	    if (cmderr != 0u)
202	        throw std::runtime_error(
203	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
204	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
205	}
206	
207	// vtype encoding for e8, m8, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=011, vta=1, vma=1). The
208	// V-data sweep uses LMUL=8 so one vle8.v/vse8.v moves a whole group of 8
209	// registers (8*vlenb byte-elements, vl=8*vlenb) in a single instruction.
210	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u;
211	
212	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
213	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
214	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
215	template<typename Bus>
216	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
217	{
218	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
219	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
220	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
221	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
222	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
223	                     "write_register_abstract");
224	}
225	
226	// Program-Buffer block sweep: seed integer base register `base_gpr` with
227	// `base_gpa`, then run `encode(reg, base_gpr, (reg-first_reg)*8)` for reg in
228	// [first_reg, last_reg) through the Program Buffer, batched at (progbufsize-1)
229	// instructions per execution (one slot reserved for the terminating ebreak).
230	// One uniform load/store encoder drives it, so the GPR/FPR restore (ld/fld,
231	// scratch -> regfile) and the GPR/FPR drain (sd/fsd, regfile -> scratch) share
232	// one implementation: ~32 registers move in ~6 halted-hart round-trips instead
233	// of ~32 abstract commands, and the values ride the shared scratch page, not
234	// DMI. The 8-byte-strided offset spans every slot (<= 248, within ld/sd's
235	// signed 12-bit immediate). The caller guarantees base_gpr is safe to seed: on
236	// a load it may be a swept register that rides LAST (its own load runs after
237	// every other use of it as the base); on a store it must be EXCLUDED from
238	// [first_reg, last_reg) -- seeding destroys its value before it could be stored
239	// -- and captured separately.
240	template<typename Bus>
241	inline void pb_block_sweep(Bus& bus, uint8_t base_gpr, uint64_t base_gpa,
242	                           uint8_t first_reg, uint8_t last_reg,
243	                           uint32_t (*encode)(uint8_t, uint8_t, int32_t))
244	{
245	    // The Program Buffer holds abstractcs.progbufsize entries (this DM reports
246	    // 8); reserve one slot for the terminating ebreak, so at most progbufsize-1
247	    // load/store insns per execution.
248	    const uint32_t progbufsize = (bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) >> 24) & 0x1Fu;
249	    const std::size_t max_ops = (progbufsize > 1) ? progbufsize - 1u : 1u;
250	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(base_gpr), base_gpa);  // base pointer

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).

# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }

      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"

      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"

fi

159	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
160	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
161	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
162	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
163	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
164	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
165	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
166	run_one() {
167	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
168	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
169	  local start end elapsed status rc
170	  start=$(date +%s)
171	  set +e
172	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
173	  rc=$?
174	  set -e
175	  end=$(date +%s)
176	  elapsed=$((end - start))
177	  case $rc in
178	    0)  status=PASS ;;
179	    77) status=SKIP ;;
180	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
181	  esac
182	  (
183	    flock 9
184	    case "$status" in
185	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
186	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
187	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
188	    esac
189	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
190	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
191	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
192	}
193	
194	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
195	# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
196	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
197	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
198	for tm in marker pc; do
199	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
200	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
201	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
202	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
203	    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
204	    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
205	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
206	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
207	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
208	  done
209	done
210	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
211	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
212	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
213	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
214	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
215	done
216	
217	# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
218	# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
219	declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
220	for tm in marker pc; do
221	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
222	  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
223	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
224	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
225	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
226	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
227	    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
228	  done
229	done

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done

TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# ROADMAP: liveness-gated transport (hybrid resume/drain)

Goal: stop paying Debug-Module traffic for state the program never changed.
Motivating profile (rt_c_hello, hybrid, --drain-minimal, ax45mpv_premium):
the vsim leg simulates 50,448 cycles for a 54-cycle ROI at ~9.8 kHz (5.2 s
wall). Split: Andes CSR block 15,235 cy / floor 13,334 cy / M-ext CSR block
9,622 cy / V transport 6,959 cy / FPR block 5,298 cy. Each DM operation
(abstract command or PB exec) costs ~200-900 simulated cycles.

Mechanism: compare each drained value against the ENGINE's own reset value
(a `hybrid_state_v1` baseline drained from the engine at reset). Equal means
the write is a no-op -- skip it. This is verify-transparent by construction
and self-heals QEMU-vs-engine reset divergence (msp_bound, milmb, ...).
mstatus-liveness (FS/VS == Off) was measured useless for C programs: hello
drains FS=Initial, VS=Clean with all-zero FPR/V data.

Known-limit notes:
- The opt-in CSR sweep (`set_csr_sweep`, currently OFF) bypasses the gate;
  filter its addr list by baseline before ever enabling it.
- Write-order hazards (mcounterwen gating counter writes) exist today in the
  tolerant path and are neither fixed nor worsened by gating; tracked by the
  separate caps/ordering audit (0x7D1 mis-gate).

## Features

### LG1: baseline-gated tolerant CSR restore -- state: DONE
- Description: `ResumeDriver::set_reset_baseline(state)` + skip every
  `write_csr_tolerant` call site (9 base scalars, Andes X-list, PMA loops,
  M-ext X-list) whose value equals the baseline. Never gated: mstatus, dpc,
  GPRs, mcycle, minstret, dcsr, S/U PMP mirror. `baseline_skip_count()`
  exposes the elision count for tests/logs. Dormant until LG3 wires a
  baseline in.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`,
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: none.

### LG2: baseline-gated FPR / V block skip -- state: DONE
- Description: skip the whole FPR fld-sweep + fcsr when fpr[0..31]+fcsr all
  equal the baseline; skip V staging + vle-sweep + vsetvl + vstart/vxsat/
  vxrm/vcsr when vreg bytes + V CSRs all equal the baseline. Decide whether
  the S/U PMP mirror joins the gate. Host-side staging (memcpy into scratch)
  may stay unconditional -- scratch is transport-only.
- Key files: `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`, `src/simulator.hpp` (staging),
  `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1 (shares baseline plumbing + skip counter).

### LG3: reset-baseline capture + cache -- state: DONE
- Landed notes: cache key adds the ELF identity (the hart free-runs a few
  workload insns before the DMI halt, so the halted state is per-ELF);
  capture enables mstatus.FS/VS first (reset leaves them Off and the
  fsd/vse8 capture sweeps fault otherwise); capture runs pass
  v_cfg_at_reset=false (the capture V sweep clobbers vtype/vl/vstart).
- Description: at hybrid resume the hart is freshly reset and halted -- the
  first run per engine build drains that reset state via StateDrain (~43k cy,
  one time), saves it under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/reset-<engine>-<version>
  .bin (validate magic/version + engine identity on load), and feeds it to
  ResumeDriver on every later run. `--no-reset-baseline` escape hatch.
  spdlog: cache hit/miss + skipped-write count.
- Key files: new `src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp` (key/path/load/save, unit-
  testable), `src/simulator.hpp` (`apply_resume_from_qemu`), `src/main.cpp`
  (flag), `tests/hybrid/reset_baseline.test.cpp`.
- Dependencies: LG1, LG2.

### LG4: e2e proof + docs (andesim repo) -- state: DONE
- Landed notes: full suite green with the gate live and a cold cache
  (47/47: marker 23, pc 23, neg 1); `--verify` PASS (146 fields);
  USER_GUIDE 2.4 documents the gate, `--no-reset-baseline`, and the cache
  location; andesim CLAUDE.md ResumeDriver bullet updated.
- Description: full `scripts/run_e2e.sh` + `--verify` matrix green; re-run
  the hello profile and record the new cycle split; update
  `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` (first-run baseline capture note, escape hatch);
  driver-side no code change expected.
- Key files: `andesim/docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, `andesim/scripts/run_e2e.sh` logs.
- Dependencies: LG3.

---
name: premium-mext-csr-capability
description: which writable M-mode CSRs the premium engine can actually verify in the hybrid handoff
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9fb5c597-ba1e-4046-8ada-d69e84b4f335
---

The v4 M-ext CSR transport (`HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`, 51 CSRs) is capability-gated.
On `ax45mpv_premium` (M-only, priv=1) only **17** are implemented and thus
round-trip-verifiable: the perf-counter set (mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6,
mhpmevent3-6, mcounterwen, mcounterinten), mdcause, and the 5 trigger CSRs
(tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext). Premium enables exactly these via
PERF_MONITOR + TRIGGER + ALWAYS gates; the other 34 are gated OFF (UMODE/SMODE/
EXCSLVL/SMRNMI/CLIC/SMSTATEEN/CCTL/PPI/FIO/EPMP all absent in its config.inc).

Key gotcha: QEMU's `andes-ax45mpv` models full S+U+M and EXPOSES CSRs (menvcfg,
mcounteren, the U-delta block, mcctl*) that vsim premium does NOT implement.
QEMU-gdbstub-exposes != vsim-implements; restoring a CSR vsim lacks can stall the
DM. So capability is decided from vsim's config.inc (andes_caps_from_config), not
from what QEMU drains. `mhpmcounter3-6` are HW counters that increment during the
ROI, so they are transported+restored but verify-EXCLUDED (like mcycle/mip).

To dump an engine's real exposed CSR set, speak RSP qXfer:features:read:
riscv-csr.xml to its gdbstub. Related: [[andes-engine-config-source]].

content.text:
Done. The 0x7D1 fix alone was not enough - enabling the sweep uncovered a second over-claim (`jvt`), now also fixed, and the drain-side CSR sweep is live with everything green.

## What landed (vsim repo, `qemu-isa-match`, 5 commits)

- `a0357df` **fix(caps)**: `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1) moved to the UMODE gate (SPA: needs PMNDS AND User mode, like its twins 0x7D3/0x7CE). The old test modeled premium's perf monitor as off - the empirical probe had blamed the wrong feature; the helper now matches the real config.inc (`PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT=1`, `PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`).
- `d4bfcf6` **feat(pb)**: a faulting sweep batch is now bisected - the error names the offending CSR instead of a bare `cmderr=3`. This is what found the second bug in one run.
- `292a560` **fix(caps)**: `jvt` (0x017) is Zcmt's table-jump base, not part of classic CoDense (`exec.it`+`uitb`). New `ZCMT` gate, off on every current engine (no config.inc carries a Zcmt knob).
- `21e8060` **feat(drain)**: `set_block_store_drain` now also enables the CSR sweep - full drains batch the Andes+M-ext block at 3 CSRs per Program-Buffer execution instead of one abstract read each. The simulator lifts the swept values from the scratch page; the lift is gated off on minimal drains (nothing sweeps there, so the region holds garbage). The restore-side sweep stays off (`csrrw` can fault on read-only fields).
- `2385278` **docs**: ROADMAP known-limits updated.

## Why the bugs were invisible before

The abstract path *tolerates* a missing CSR: `read_register_64` clears the fault and mirrors it as zero - and QEMU drains zero too, so `--verify` falsely matched. The batched sweep is all-or-nothing, which makes it the first real validator of the caps table. Both over-claimed CSRs were "verified" for months while never actually existing on premium.

## Results

- Unit suite 26/26; e2e **47/47** (marker 23, pc 23, neg 1) with fresh baseline captures on both engines.
- Hello `--verify` PASS: **144 fields** (was 146 - exactly the two de-claimed CSRs), window still 54 cycles.
- Warm timings: plain hybrid 1.7 s, `--verify` 5.1 s, cold capture+verify 8.5 s.
- andesim repo: USER_GUIDE performance note updated (uncommitted - the file has your pre-existing edits mixed in, same as the earlier 2.4 changes). The CSR coverage guard still passes; the matrix tracks the wire format, which didn't change.
